lines: Welcome to Module Four: Fine-Tuning.
You'll learn when to fine-tune, and how to do it well on one GPU.

say.1: You'll learn when to fine-tune, and how to do it well on one G P U.

lines: Picture an insurance company whose support assistant keeps going off script.
It rambles, ignores the house tone, and breaks the ticket format.
The team's first instinct is to fine-tune it on every policy document.
But policies change weekly, so the model would be stale by Monday.
Lesson one sorts the levers, from prompting and RAG to full fine-tuning.
Missing knowledge needs retrieval; behaviour, format, and style need fine-tuning.

say.0: Lesson one sorts the levers, from prompting and rag to full fine-tuning.

lines: So the team keeps RAG for facts, and fine-tunes for behaviour.
Lesson two's lab runs supervised fine-tuning of a small Qwen model with TRL.

say.0: So the team keeps rag for facts, and fine-tunes for behaviour.
say.1: Lesson two's lab runs supervised fine-tuning of a small Chwen model with T R L.

lines: You'll train only on the assistant's replies, with the right chat template.
Then you'll compare outputs before and after, and read the loss curves.
But fully fine-tuning a seven billion parameter model needs over a hundred gigabytes.
That's where LoRA comes in.
LoRA freezes the base model and trains two small matrices beside each layer.
Only a tiny fraction of the weights learn, and the adapter is just megabytes.

say.0: Lora freezes the base model and trains two small matrices beside each layer.

lines: QLoRA goes further, loading the frozen base in four-bit precision.
In the lab, you'll QLoRA-tune Qwen on a free Colab T4, then merge the adapter.

say.0: Cue lora goes further, loading the frozen base in four-bit precision.
say.1: In the lab, you'll cue lora tune Chwen on a free Colab T four, then merge the adapter.

lines: Now the format is right, but reviewers still prefer some answers over others.
Lesson four turns those preferences into a training signal.
Classic RLHF trains a reward model, then optimizes with PPO.
DPO skips the reward model and learns straight from chosen and rejected pairs.

say.0: Classic R L H F trains a reward model, then optimizes with P P O.
say.1: D P O skips the reward model and learns straight from chosen and rejected pairs.

lines: GRPO scores a group of sampled answers against each other.
With checkable rewards it's powerful, but watch for reward hacking.

say.0: G R P O scores a group of sampled answers against each other.

lines: Lesson five maps it all to NVIDIA NeMo, at cluster scale.
You'll compare p-tuning, adapters, IA3, and LoRA by where they add parameters.

say.1: You'll compare P tuning, adapters, I A three, and lora by where they add parameters.

lines: You'll also guard against catastrophic forgetting, where new skills erase old ones.
Lower learning rates, fewer epochs, and mixed-in general data protect old skills.
Fine-tuning is thirteen percent of the exam.
Expect method choice, LoRA memory math, and DPO versus RLHF.

say.1: Expect method choice, lora memory math, and D P O versus R L H F.

lines: By the end, you'll fine-tune, align, and ship a small model on a single GPU.
Let's begin with lesson one: choosing an adaptation method.
